title: Mindfulness as a Protective Factor in Multiple Sclerosis Revisited
abstract: Abstract: Mindfulness has been linked to lower fatigue in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS). Prior work suggests that depression may mediate this relationship. This study examined the mediating role of depression in 103 PwMS who completed measures of mindfulness, depression, fatigue, and a walking task to induce motor fatigue. Higher mindfulness and lower depression were associated with reduced self-reported fatigue. Mediation analyses showed that mindfulness was not directly related to fatigue, but that depression functioned as a mediator. Consistent with this, mindfulness was not related to objective motor fatigue, whereas it was related to subjective fatigue. Mindfulness might hence ease the subjective burden of fatigue by reducing depressive symptoms rather than altering fatigability itself. Integrative neuropsychological therapy should hence emphasize mindfulness and acceptance of fatigue in PwMS.
